title: Observability pipeline debug notes - tracing/metrics/logs (Ryan)
content:
Context:
- Intermittent drop in traces and metrics for hosted-api ingestion pipeline starting ~2025-02-10 18:00 UTC. Logs continue to appear, but traces often missing parent spans and metrics counters show null/0 for short intervals. Affects ~2-5% of requests, spike correlated with high write throughput bursts.

Hypothesis/observations so far:
- Suspect rate-limiting or backpressure in the trace agent (otel-collector) causing batch flush to drop.
- Alternatively, trace sampling config might be dynamically switching (bug in config reload).
- Some ingestion workers (k8s pods) show higher GC/pause times - possible that KV cache flush path blocks exporter.

Quick checks / commands run (notes):
1) Check otel-collector logs for exporter errors (grep for "exporter" / "failed"):
   kubectl -n observability logs deploy/otel-collector | grep -i "export" | tail -n 200
   -> saw repeated: "failed to export spans: resource exhausted" around 2025-02-10T18:03:45Z

2) Look for sampling config reloads in collector:
   kubectl -n observability logs -l app=otel-collector --since=24h | grep -E "config.*reload|reload.*sampl"
   -> no explicit reload events, but noticed: "error reading config: EOF" at 18:03:44Z followed by "using last known config" message.

3) Metrics from collector pod (prom endpoint):
   kubectl -n observability port-forward svc/otel-collector 8888:8888 &
   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/metrics | grep -E "exporter|batch|queue|dropped"
   -> exporter_queue_dropped_total increased by ~1200 during spike window.

4) Check worker pods for OOM/GC pauses:
   kubectl -n ingest top pods --containers | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 10
   -> several ingest-worker-* pods at 85-92% memory. No recent OOMKilled events recorded.

5) Inspect logs for "span dropped" or "dropped spans due to queue"
   kubectl -n ingest logs -l app=ingest-worker --since=3h | grep -i "span drop\|dropped span\|queue full"
   -> multiple lines: "warning: exporter queue is full, dropping 50 spans" (timestamps match gaps)

6) Repro curl to ingestion endpoint with tracing header to see if spans are created and flushed:
   curl -vv -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" -X POST https://hosted-api.redwood.test/ingest -d '{"test":"payload"}' | jq .
   -> Response 200, but trace not visible in traces UI within 30s. Search for trace id returned no spans.

Error snippets collected:
- "failed to export spans: resource exhausted" - otel exporter (stdout)
- "exporter queue is full, dropping 50 spans" - ingest worker
- "error reading config: EOF" - otel collector config loader
- "http2: stream error: stream ID 25; REFUSED_STREAM" - grpc exporter failures in collector

Config bits to inspect (files / env):
- otel-collector configmap: kubectl -n observability get configmap otel-collector-config -o yaml
  * batching processor settings: timeout, send_batch_size, send_batch_max_size, queue_size
- exporter (gRPC) settings: max_concurrent_streams, retry_on_failure, backoff settings
- ingest-worker exporter queue length env var: EXPORTER_QUEUE_LIMIT (defaults 1024)
- sampling config path (file reload) and SIGHUP handler for collector image

Short-term mitigation attempted:
- Increase queue_size/batching send_batch_size + restart otel-collector (rolling) to see if dropped count reduces.
  - kubectl apply -f otel-collector-configmap-updated.yaml -> applied. Rolling restart: kubectl -n observability rollout restart deploy/otel-collector
  - After restart, exporter_queue_dropped_total stopped increasing for 20 minutes, but then resumed on next throughput burst.
- Enable temporary logging at DEBUG for collector to capture more detail (will increase noise).
- Scale ingest-worker deployment from 6 -> 10 pods (HPA scaled earlier but surge caused pods to lag on image pull).

Longer-term investigations / tasks:
- Reproduce load in staging with similar burst profile (sine wave to simulate traffic). Measure queue depth and flush latency.
- Add per-request span size metric to detect oversized spans that block exporter.
- Evaluate moving exporter to async buffered agent with bigger disk-backed queue for durability.
- Add backpressure metric export to SLO monitoring (alerts when exporter_queue_dropped_total > X over 5m).
- Check TLS/gRPC keepalive settings - saw REFUSED_STREAM, might be hitting max concurrent streams on backend (collector -> storage).

Notes / breadcrumbs from infra team (Slack snippets):
- Priya: "saw a bump in GC for ingest-worker around the same time, investigating memory leak in message parsing" (2025-02-11 01:12)
- Eli: "collector config reloads aren't atomic in current image - if file write is interrupted we get EOF and collector falls back to previous config" (2025-02-12 09:03)

Commands to run next (checklist):
- [ ] Add 'queue_length' gauge to ingest-worker debug logs and ship to debug metrics index.
- [ ] Run k6 synthetic burst test in staging (payloads similar to production) and capture exporter_queue_dropped_total, span flush latency.
- [ ] Increase otel collector exporter max_concurrent_streams on backend (storage proxy) and test under load.
- [ ] Check gRPC library version in collector image, compare to upstream bugfixes for REFUSED_STREAM issues.
- [ ] Add alert: exporter_queue_dropped_total > 100 in 5m -> paging policy.

Quick reproduction script (staging):
- k6 script: endpoints= ["/ingest", "/ingest"] ; ramp up to 1200 rps for 60s -> check metrics. (script saved in /ops/load/observability-burst-k6.js)

Trace IDs observed during incident (samples):
- 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 (no spans in UI) 2025-02-10T18:04:12Z
- 6f1d5cfb9a2b4b9b8c3a7d9e0f123456 (partial spans, missing parent) 2025-02-10T18:04:47Z

Quick notes to self for postmortem:
- Timeline: 2025-02-10 18:00 UTC traffic surge -> first dropped exporter messages at 18:03:45Z -> temporary collector restart at 18:20 -> partial recovery -> resumed drops at 19:05 -> scale up and config change at 19:30 -> metrics normalized by 20:10 but traces still missing intermittently until 2025-02-11 02:00 when code fix deployed to ingest-worker.
- Owner for follow-up: Priya (ingest parsing memory), Eli (collector config reload + image update), Ryan (alerts + staging repro)

Random notes / ideas:
- Consider switching from synchronous gRPC exporter to HTTP/1.1 with retry buffer for large bursts - tradeoffs around performance.
- Add 'span_size' histogram to detect any anomalous spans that are 10x normal size.
- For critical routes, add a lightweight spanning header that forces sampling to 1.0 so we can validate end-to-end.

End of notes (will consolidate into postmortem template once repro confirmed).
